alternatives.root_cause: Ad's process was stopped while its socket still accepted, causing callers to hang to deadline.
alternatives.why_not: A frozen process writes nothing; ad kept emitting log lines well after onset (tr_0e838a0945c8), including active outbound connection attempts.

alternatives.root_cause: A flagd-driven flag enabled a failing or slow code path inside ad.
alternatives.why_not: flagd resolution calls on the cart path completed in well under a millisecond inside healthy traces (tr_13fba48925a2), and the ad hang shows no ad span executing at all, so no flagged ad code path is running.

alternatives.root_cause: A downstream dependency of ad became slow and ad blocked waiting on it.
alternatives.why_not: Dependency latency would still produce ad spans with long durations; instead ad produced no spans in the affected traces and its log reports inability to resolve a host rather than slow responses.

verdict.summary: The ad service lost network reachability around 01:52, so ad-serving requests hung until the 15s client deadline while ad's own process kept running and logged that it could not resolve/reach other hosts.
verdict.reasoning: Ad's error-ratio did not rise; instead intervals with no traffic at all appeared in the incident window (tr_f9dd4904182e), which is the signature of requests never completing rather than failing. Traces show ad-path requests from load-generator through frontend-proxy and frontend hanging to a flat ~15.0s deadline and erroring at the caller, with no ad span present at all in those traces, while every non-ad path (cart, product-catalog, checkout, currency, flagd) stayed in the single-digit-millisecond range (tr_13fba48925a2); ad spans exist only before onset (tr_290ba495d347). Ad is not silent: its own log continues after onset and complains that it cannot reach a remote host by name (tr_0e838a0945c8), which distinguishes a partitioned-but-running process from a frozen one. No deploy or config change was recorded for ad or flagd (tr_396ba943d492, tr_92b96600c364), ruling out bad_deploy, bad_config, and a flag flip on the ad path. The alerting order (frontend-proxy first) is caller-side propagation: proxy and load-generator merely noticed the hang.
open_questions: Whether the partition is DNS-only or full L3 isolation — the observed failure is name resolution for an outbound host, and inbound reachability from frontend was not directly tested.
Whether ad's inbound socket still accepts connections (frontend logs were empty, tr_5d5c137f2b2f, so the client-side error text is unknown).
The exact onset boundary for ad's traffic gaps was not pinned to the second.
